attacker.model: claude (Kiro subagent; exact model version not exposed to the agent)

null-vs-empty.notApplicableReason: Every text column the view reads (Product.Name, ProductModel.Name, ProductDescription.Description, CultureID) is NOT NULL, so no NULL text value can be sent; '' is attacked in its own case.

cases.label: culture codes differing only in case or by a trailing space ('en', 'EN', 'en '), an empty code and a six-character code
cases.reasoning: CultureID is nchar(6) and not compared in the view. 'en' and 'EN' are two rows with their own spelling, on different descriptions because the source key (ProductModelID, ProductDescriptionID, CultureID) is case-insensitive; 'en ' pads to the same value as 'en' (six characters) on both engines; '' pads to six spaces.

cases.label: descriptions with an emoji, combining accents, right-to-left text, CR LF and a tab, leading and trailing spaces, and 400 characters
cases.reasoning: Description is nvarchar(400) (varchar(400) on PostgreSQL). Supplementary characters are two UTF-16 units on SQL Server and one code point on PostgreSQL; the 400-character value uses only BMP characters so it fits both. Line breaks and tabs must survive the load scripts on both engines.

cases.label: an empty description, and product and model names that differ only in case from each other: '' kept, not NULL
cases.reasoning: Every text column is NOT NULL, so '' is the only empty value; it must not become NULL. Product names and model names are each unique in the source, so the case-only pairs are across the two tables: product 'Chain' on model 'CHAIN', product 'road' on model 'Road'. The view compares no text; both spellings are passed through unchanged.

cases.label: two descriptions with the same text in one culture and two products on one model: rows multiply (2 products x 3 culture rows), identical rows kept
cases.reasoning: The view does not return ProductDescriptionID, so descriptions 1 and 3, both 'same' and both in culture 'en', give two identical rows per product from distinct source keys; there is no DISTINCT. Two products (distinct names, as the source requires) of one model fan out over all its culture rows. Compared as a multiset.

top-ties.detail: two rows of Production.Product share ProductModelID = 1

cases.label: keys with gaps and at the int limits: product 2147483647, model -2147483648, description 0; a NULL model and a dangling description dropped
cases.reasoning: ProductID, ProductModelID and ProductDescriptionID are keys with gaps and type extremes. Product 5 has ProductModelID NULL (inner join drops it); a culture row points at missing description 99 (dropped).

objections.text: The rows (ProductModelID 1, ProductDescriptionID 1, CultureID 'en') and the same tuple with CultureID 'EN' collide under the source case-insensitive composite primary key; nchar padding also applies. Both rows cannot coexist under the source schema preconditions.
objections.resolution: A01 now assigns 'en' and 'EN' to different ProductDescriptionID values, so the composite keys are distinct while both stored culture spellings are projected.

objections.text: Product names 'Chain' and 'CHAIN' collide under the source case-insensitive unique key on Product.Name, and model names 'Road' and 'ROAD' collide under the corresponding ProductModel.Name key. The case-only rows cannot coexist in source data.
objections.resolution: A03 now places each case-only pair across Product.Name and ProductModel.Name rather than within one uniquely constrained column. Product names and model names are each unique under the source collation.

objections.text: A04 duplicates the exact ProductModelProductDescriptionCulture primary-key tuple (1, 1, 'en'), and the two products both use Name 'Bike' despite the source unique key on Product.Name. The claimed duplicate fan-out input is outside the source schema preconditions.
objections.resolution: A04 now uses distinct product names and distinct description ids for the equal description text. Every culture bridge key is distinct, while two descriptions still project identical rows per product.
